questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If it loses pressure, the emergency brakes on the trailer will automatically activate.

questions.question: Combination vehicles require:

options.text: Less skill than single commercial vehicles.
The same skill as single commercial vehicles.
More skill than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More skill than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more driving skill. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rollovers?

options.text: Keep the load toward the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, load cargo as low as possible and take turns slowly.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, you should:

options.text: Any glad hand can connect to any other.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: Always connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to prevent mistakes. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, first turn the steering wheel:

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to go.
In the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the wheel opposite to your desired direction first. Once the trailer begins to turn, turn the wheel in the other direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: Before driving, how do you check that air reaches all trailers?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Disconnect the air supply lines and listen for escaping air.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Wait for air pressure to build up. Then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes, air is reaching all trailers.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, you should NOT:

options.text: Let the wheels grip the road.

questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels regain traction. Do not apply the trailer hand brake because braking is what caused the skid.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, you should:

options.text: Connect the correct glad hand pairs.
Leave one pair of glad hands loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hand pairs.
questions.explanation: Always connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are often color-coded to help prevent mistakes. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: If a trailer is too high:
questions.explanation: The trailer must be at the correct height when coupling. If it is too low, the trailer nose may be damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple properly.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, the driver:

options.text: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
Can use the parking brake to straighten the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels regain traction. Do not apply the trailer hand brake because braking caused the wheels to lock.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to flip over from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: If you drive a vehicle made before 1998 and are not sure if the trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what can you do?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to turn on the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes.
questions.explanation: If you drive a vehicle made before 1998 and are not sure if the trailer has ABS, look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle is lightly loaded, what happens?

options.text: The brakes do not work as well.
Most weight should be in the back of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes do not work as well.
questions.explanation: When a combination vehicle is lightly loaded, the tires have poor grip on the road. The wheels can lock up easily when you stop a light vehicle.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?

options.text: A five-axle tractor with one trailer
A three-axle tractor with one trailer

questions.explanation: Triple trailers are most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer during coupling, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Coupling and uncoupling trailers safely is important for operating a combination vehicle. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, send air to the trailer.

questions.question: Trailers with low ground clearance can be difficult to drive over:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be difficult to cross with a low-clearance trailer. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers have special trouble crossing raised railroad tracks.

questions.question: If the air supply control is in the "emergency" position, what happens?

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will lock.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will lock.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have air supply controls operated by levers instead of knobs. If the control is set to "emergency," the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes lock.

questions.question: Before you back the tractor under the trailer, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Coupling and uncoupling trailers safely is important for operating a combination vehicle. Before backing the tractor under the trailer, the trailer brakes must be locked.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your air tanks, the brakes:

options.text: Will make a loud noise when used.

questions.explanation: Drain your air tanks every day to remove water and oil. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can stop the brakes from working correctly.

questions.question: During a trip, the landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Always raise the landing gear all the way before driving. Landing gear that is not fully raised can catch on railroad tracks or other road hazards.
